euronews.description: Speaking to Euronews, Serviceplan Group CEO Florian Haller said marketing has evolved far beyond traditional advertising, and now sits at the centre of the "whole customer journey" where "data, technology and creativity" meet.

euronews.description: Construction and agriculture are Europe's most heat-exposed industries, with transport, manufacturing and energy also facing growing disruption as climate change pushes temperatures higher.

euronews.description: Thousands of Shiite Muslims marked Ashoura in Nabatieh on 26 June, holding processions through neighbourhoods devastated by recent Israeli airstrikes in a powerful display of resilience.

euronews.description: The report ranked European countries for their abundance of lakes rated as “excellent”, meaning their water quality was safe for swimming.

euronews.description: Watching tense, fast-paced football games requires focus, but so does consuming World Cup content online, because false images surrounding the tournament are becoming increasingly common.

euronews.title: 'Measures needed to face extreme heat or it will kill us,' Copernicus director says
euronews.description: As scorching weather hits Europe, climate expert Carlo Buontempo told Euronews' flagship morning show Europe Today that "record-breaking temperatures should not be breaking news" and that strategies are needed to face extreme weather lest humanity suffers the consequences.

euronews.title: Life sentence for Magdeburg attacker
euronews.description: When he drove a car into the Magdeburg Christmas market, he killed six people and injured more than 300. Taleb al Abdulmohsen has now been sentenced to life imprisonment.

euronews.title: Seismic doublet: the phenomenon that turned Venezuela's tragedy into catastrophe
euronews.description: On Wednesday 24 June 2026 at 18:04 local time, north-western Venezuela began to shake and, 39 seconds later, a second quake hit, feeding back into the first. But what exactly is a seismic doublet, and why is it so dangerous?

euronews.description: The Greek astronaut will conduct experiments and technology demonstrations proposed by dozens of Greek research teams, institutions and universities.

euronews.description: Europe is being hit by record-high temperatures in a heatwave that is expected to last for a further two weeks across the continent.

euronews.title: France’s power utility to pour €80mn to cool down schools, nurseries and daycare centers
euronews.description: France’s state-owned power utility Électricité de France (EDF) will invest €80 million to equip schools, nurseries and daycare centers with cooling systems as the country faces increasingly severe heatwaves.

rfi.title: France heatwave overwhelms hospitals and forces Pride march delay
rfi.description: Emergency doctors at one of Paris's biggest hospitals warned on Friday that wards had become dangerously overcrowded after a week of soaring temperatures, as authorities restricted public alcohol consumption, organisers postponed the annual Pride march and €130 million was pledged to help schools adapt to climate change.

rfi.title: Current Europe heatwave 'impossible' without human-induced climate change
rfi.description: A study comparing the heatwave that has swept across Europe this week with heatwaves in 1976 and 2003 has found that human-caused climate change is "unequivocally" responsible for the extreme heat over the last week – with France recording its hottest day since records began in 1947 on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Calls for child protection reforms in wake of schoolgirl Lyhanna's death
rfi.description: An investigation into previous child rape allegations against the suspect in the death of a schoolgirl in southern France has revealed failures by prosecutors and police. The case has unleashed a wave of criticism over how sexual and gender-based violence cases are handled in France, with victims, families and advocates pushing for reform.

rfi.title: Fear of mines alone could disrupt Strait of Hormuz shipping, warns French admiral
rfi.description: The Strait of Hormuz has reopened under a fragile United States-Iran deal, but it remains under close watch after maritime authorities warned of suspected and confirmed mines in the area. Former French Navy Admiral Éric Lavault – who headed France's mine warfare and seabed operations, and commanded the navy's bomb-disposal divers – told RFI that even without proof the strait has been mined, it must be checked before commercial shipping can return to normal.

rfi.title: Paris court gives oil giant TotalEnergies deadline to tighten climate policies
rfi.description: A court in Paris ruled on Thursday that energy giant TotalEnergies must account for its consumers’ greenhouse gas emissions, giving the French company six months to adjust a legally mandated risk assessment.

rfi.title: France told to do more to protect children from human trafficking
rfi.description: France must step up efforts to prevent human trafficking and improve support for victims, particularly children and young people, the Council of Europe has said, warning that weaknesses in the country's child protection system continue to leave minors exposed to exploitation.

rfi.title: Pépé stars as Cote d'Ivoire beat Curaçao to reach knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Nicolas Pépé scored twice on Thursday to fire Cote d'Ivoire to the second phase of a World Cup tournament for the first time with a 2-0 win over Curaçao.

rfi.title: Relief in sight as temperatures set to fall in France after record heatwave
rfi.description: Temperatures are expected to fall in France from Thursday evening after another day of extreme heat that put 72 of mainland France's 96 departments on red alert, affecting more than 50 million people.

rfi.title: South African anti-migrant groups defend planned ‘Liberation March’
rfi.description: A coalition of South African organisations campaigning against undocumented migrants has defended its plans for nationwide demonstrations on 30 June, insisting the marches will be peaceful despite rising tensions and recent deadly unrest.

rfi.title: Kenya mounts huge security operation on Gen Z protest anniversary
rfi.description: Kenyan police put on a massive show of force Thursday in a bid to prevent protests marking two years since a landmark Gen Z uprising.

rfi.title: Macron to host Meloni in Antibes as France and Italy seek closer ties
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron will host Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in the French seaside resort of Antibes, as the two leaders try to revive a relationship that has been marked by political differences.

rfi.title: Zelensky to miss Poland summit as Second World War row escalates
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky will not attend a major conference on rebuilding Ukraine being held in Poland this week, as a dispute between the two countries over Second World War remembrance threatens to overshadow talks.

rfi.title: South Africa beat South Korea to reach World Cup knockout stages for first time
rfi.description: Thapelo Maseko scored mid way through the second half against South Korea to take South Africa into the knockout stages at a World Cup for the first time.

rfi.title: Digital euro wins key EU backing as lawmakers approve draft rules
rfi.description: The European Union has moved a step closer to creating a digital euro, after members of the European Parliament passed a crucial vote on the virtual currency.

rfi.title: Brazil overpower Scotland to take Group C as Morocco wear down Haiti
rfi.description: Brazil outclassed Scotland 3-0 on Wednesday night in Miami to claim Group C at the 2026 World Cup. Carlo Ancelotti's men started the final round of games in pole position following their 3-0 win over Haiti on 19 June while Morocco edged past Scotland 1-0.

rfi.title: France announces first Ebola case in doctor returned from DR Congo
rfi.description: French health authorities on Wednesday announced the first confirmed case of Ebola identified on national territory – a doctor who had returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

rfi.title: US releases experimental Ebola drug for DR Congo outbreak trials
rfi.description: Experimental Ebola drugs are being shipped to Democratic Republic of Congo as the United States releases doses of a treatment for clinical trials in a widening outbreak that has caused more than 1,000 cases and over 250 deaths, the World Health Organization and US officials have said.

rfi.title: Switzerland outwit Canada to claim Group B at 2026 World Cup
rfi.description: Switzerland claimed top spot in Group B at the World Cup on Wednesday following a 2-1 win over Canada in Vancouver.

lemonde.title: « S’ils nous avaient mis des volets, on ne souffrirait pas comme ça » : la canicule à La Courneuve et à Saint-Denis, entre colère, débrouille et entraide
lemonde.description: Au cœur de deux grands ensembles bétonnés de Seine-Saint-Denis, la vie s’est transformée depuis une semaine, du fait des chaleurs extrêmes. Les habitants racontent leurs difficultés et leur ras-le-bol.

lemonde.title: Séismes au Venezuela : le bilan s’alourdit à 589 morts et près de 3 000 blessés
lemonde.description: Les recherches se poursuivent dans les décombres d’immeubles qui se sont effondrés pour tenter de secourir des personnes prises au piège, au lendemain d’un double séisme extrêmement puissant.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : la Crimée déclarée en « situation d’urgence » par les autorités russes
lemonde.description: La Crimée, annexée par la Russie en 2014, est en proie à une crise du carburant, qui s’est aggravée ces derniers jours en raison de coupures d’électricité généralisées dans toutes les parties de la péninsule, y compris à Sébastopol, à la suite d’attaques de drones ukrainiens.

lemonde.title: Ebola : après un premier cas diagnostiqué en France chez un médecin de retour de RDC, la surveillance s’organise
lemonde.description: Le médecin infecté avait été envoyé par l’ONG française Alima en Ituri, une province de l’Est congolais foyer de l’épidémie, pour participer à la riposte sanitaire contre le virus.

lemonde.title: France-Norvège : Erling Haaland et ses coéquipiers, purs produits de la fabrique à champions d’un pays qui mise sur le sport
lemonde.description: En Norvège, dont l’équipe nationale affronte la France, vendredi, en phase de groupes de la Coupe du monde 2026, le sport fait partie de l’identité nationale. Le pays ne cesse de sortir des champions, dans de nombreuses disciplines. Les acteurs de cette réussite ont livré au « Monde » les secrets de leur méthode.

lemonde.title: Vacances à l’étranger : comment réduire vos frais bancaires ?
lemonde.description: Les banques de réseaux facturent des frais lors de chaque opération par carte bancaire en dehors de la zone euro. Des solutions existent toutefois pour limiter la note.

lemonde.title: A Narbonne, Louis, 17 ans, meurt à la suite d’une violente agression filmée
lemonde.description: La victime a été violemment passée à tabac par plusieurs jeunes, vendredi 19 juin, avant de succomber à ses blessures quelques jours plus tard. Cinq jeunes ont été interpellés, puis mis en examen, mardi, pour tentative d’assassinat, et placés en détention provisoire.

lemonde.title: Au Brésil, la famille Bolsonaro se déchire avant l’élection présidentielle d’octobre
lemonde.description: Michelle Bolsonaro, épouse de l’ancien président d’extrême droite et figure appréciée des évangéliques, a accusé publiquement son beau-fils Flavio, qui souhaite affronter le président sortant Lula, de lui avoir « manqué de respect ».

lemonde.title: Financière et politique, la double fragilisation de la recherche publique
lemonde.description: Les universités et les organismes de recherche voient leur trésorerie se dégrader. Une situation inquiétante pour l’avenir, analyse le journaliste David Larousserie. D’autant que malgré les discours officiels faisant de la recherche une priorité, de plus en plus de décisions politiques font fi de l’état des connaissances scientifiques.

lemonde.title: A Biarritz, l’effondrement d’une falaise, reflet de l’érosion de la côte basque
lemonde.description: Quelque 2 000 mètres cubes de cailloux et de terre ont été précipités dans l’océan, mercredi, dans la station balnéaire basque, tuant une plongeuse. Un autre plongeur est porté disparu. Comme le littoral aquitain landais et girondin plus au nord, cette portion de côte est de plus en plus soumise aux assauts de la mer.

lemonde.title: Guillaume Erner s’excuse après la diffusion d’un audio « fallacieux », sans satisfaire Jean-Luc Mélenchon
lemonde.description: Au cours d’un entretien avec Marine Le Pen, l’animateur a diffusé mercredi l’extrait dans lequel on entendait en parallèle la description que Jean-Marie Le Pen faisait des juifs et des propos de Jean-Luc Mélenchon censés s’en rapprocher.

lemonde.title: Un an après avoir remplacé Wagner, les Russes d’Africa Corps en difficulté au Mali
lemonde.description: « Mali : un an d’Africa Corps » (1/2). Des attaques de djihadistes et d’indépendantistes touareg dans plusieurs régions du pays ont ébranlé, fin avril, la junte au pouvoir.

lemonde.title: La mort de Gérard Brémond, père visionnaire du groupe Pierre & Vacances
lemonde.description: L’inventeur du concept de « nouvelle propriété » avait aussi créé la station de ski d’Avoriaz puis son Festival du film fantastique. Il s’est éteint le 25 juin à 88 ans.

lemonde.title: La Suède discrimine les migrants d’origine rom en leur refusant des soins, selon le Conseil de l’Europe
lemonde.description: Une réclamation avait été déposée en 2023 par les ONG Amnesty International et Médecins du Monde. Selon les experts, Stockhom contrevient à trois des dispositions de la Charte sociale européenne.

lemonde.title: La ville de Brest approuve la création d’une police municipale, promesse de campagne du maire
lemonde.description: Deuxième ville de Bretagne, Brest était la dernière ville de plus de 100 000 habitants en France à être dépourvue d’une telle force. L’édile Stéphane Roudaut a chiffré sa mise en place à 7 millions d’euros par an.

lemonde.description: L’édile d’extrême droite Steeve Briois a suspendu sans traitement deux agents encartés à SUD, malgré l’avis négatif du conseil de discipline. « Pure discrimination syndicale », selon l’avocat des plaignants.

lemonde.title: L’album « The Wow ! Signal » du groupe Muse, à la rencontre de trois types perdus dans le cosmos

new-sci.description: An instrument on the Perseverance rover has identified large, complex carbon compounds alongside unusual patterns on the surface of rocks that resemble traces of microbial activity

new-sci.title: Screwworm could be the first species targeted by an 'extinction drive'

new-sci.title: All known Homo naledi skeletons seem to be female
new-sci.description: An analysis of tooth proteins suggests all 23 Homo naledi individuals found in the Rising Star cave in South Africa were female, which strengthens the case that they were placed there deliberately

phys-org.title: When a pool or pond turns green with algae, don't reach for chemicals—nature has better solutions
phys-org.description: When the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool turned green with algae just days after a US$15 million renovation, the U.S. government scrambled for chemicals and expensive technical solutions to fix the iconic landmark.

phys-org.title: A single origin story for the Milky Way's most mysterious stars
phys-org.description: Lurking at the heart of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) is a supermassive black hole four million times the mass of the sun, surrounded by a puzzling collection of young, massive stars whose orbits have long defied explanation. Astronomers have proposed various competing theories to account for these stars, but none has been able to explain all of them together.

phys-org.title: How bacteria use circadian clocks to colonize their world
phys-org.description: Research has revealed how bacteria rely on circadian clocks to control the spread of their multicellular colonies. The findings provide important clues as to how we might improve soil health and plant growth. They may also help explain how some bacteria spread hospital-acquired infections. Researchers at the John Innes Center, University of Munich and Leiden University made the discovery while studying the widespread soil bacterium Bacillus subtilis.

phys-org.title: Scientists find antidepressant in the brains of sharks off the coast of Rio de Janeiro
phys-org.description: Sertraline is one of the most widely prescribed antidepressants in the world. Global sertraline sales are expected to keep growing, projected to expand from an estimated US$1.94 billion in 2025 to approximately US$3.13 billion by 2032.

phys-org.title: The US and China are planning moon bases: Designs may cut construction waste and improve life on Earth
phys-org.description: The NASA Artemis program, now supported by 67 countries under the Artemis Accords, plans to return humans to the moon by 2028. A recent White House Executive Order has gone further, directing NASA to establish a permanent lunar outpost by 2030.

phys-org.title: Most bees are solitary and don't live in hives: How climate change risks them starving
phys-org.description: When we think of bees, we often think of flowers. The more flowers, the better, right? Well, not exactly. Like us, bees need to consume specific nutrients in suitable amounts and combinations.

phys-org.title: Flooding rains, ocean gains: How a huge Murray flood gave the sea a feast
phys-org.description: For decades, the rivers of the Murray-Darling Basin have been heavily regulated by dams and irrigation networks. As a result, the volume of water entering the ocean is about 60% smaller than 100 years ago. But nature broke through during massive floods over the summer of 2022–23, when heavy rains filled the basin's waterways.

phys-org.title: First Nations women in fire: A vital opportunity to boost the workforce and increase community safety
phys-org.description: A groundbreaking report has revealed that supporting First Nations women in fire and land management is a critical, yet untapped, strategy for protecting Australian communities from escalating climate disasters.

phys-org.title: Metal hydride molecule trapped with laser light opens path to ultracold hydrogen
phys-org.description: Controlling and trapping molecules, units of a substance consisting of two or more chemically bound atoms, with laser light is significantly more challenging than trapping individual atoms. This is because molecules exhibit more complex vibrational and rotational dynamics that make them more difficult to cool and trap.

phys-org.title: New research outlines human-centered AI framework for online student success
phys-org.description: University of Phoenix College of Doctoral Studies scholars Pamayla E. Darbyshire, DHA, MSN/CNS, and Carl Beitsayadeh, MS, have published the article, "Enhancing Student Success through GAI and Predictive Analytics," in International Journal for Educational Media and Technology, an issue that featured refereed papers originally presented at the 2025 Teaching, Colleges, and Community Worldwide Online Conference (TCC).

phys-org.title: Study challenges idea that simply playing sports makes kids less prone to violent behavior
phys-org.description: Contrary to popular belief, simply playing organized youth sports does not reduce the likelihood of committing violence in one's lifetime and, in some cases, may increase it, according to a new study.

phys-org.title: Sea anemones reveal antiviral defense that reverses human immune playbook
phys-org.description: A new study has uncovered a previously unknown antiviral defense mechanism in sea anemones, revealing that animals may have evolved more than one way to fight viral infections. Researchers discovered that a protein resembling a key component of the human immune system actually plays the opposite role, yet remains essential for effective antiviral protection.

phys-org.title: How a 'copper economy' helps fungi and bacteria build stubborn biofilms
phys-org.description: Scientists have discovered that two common human pathogens can work together by managing copper in their shared environment—a finding that could open new ways to break down stubborn mixed biofilms.

phys-org.title: Scientists find evidence of vast hidden magma systems inside Mars
phys-org.description: Researchers from the University of Oxford have uncovered evidence that Mars once hosted enormous, Earth-like magmatic systems deep beneath its surface—despite the planet lacking the plate tectonics long thought necessary for this kind of geological complexity.

phys-org.title: Wastewater management reverses widespread freshwater deoxygenation in China
phys-org.description: Freshwater ecosystems worldwide have been suffering from declining oxygen levels—a trend known as deoxygenation—that threatens biodiversity, fisheries and ecosystem stability. However, a new study published in Nature Geoscience offers hope: targeted nutrient management via wastewater control can reverse this trajectory, even in the face of rapid climate warming.

phys-org.title: What to know about earthquake early warning systems
phys-org.description: As earthquakes struck from California to Venezuela to Japan, millions of people received warnings on their mobile phones, providing critical seconds to seek protection.

phys-org.title: Europe's extreme heat would be impossible without climate change, scientists say
phys-org.description: The record-breaking heat that's scorching Europe day and night this month would not have been possible without climate change, according to a new study.

phys-org.title: Hospitals overwhelmed as Europe heat wave shifts east
phys-org.description: A deadly European heat wave that has saturated hospitals as temperatures soared to record highs was shifting east Friday, with authorities warning of more misery on a continent not used to stretches of punishing heat.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

undark.title: Advocacy Groups Express Mixed Views on Embryo Editing
undark.description: At least two new start-up companies, Preventive and Origin Genomics, say they are developing strategies that combine gene editing with in vitro fertilization to correct disease-causing mutations. Advocacy groups for people living with these genetic disorders have been quiet on the developments.

undark.title: Interview: California Lawmaker Calls for a Peptide Working Group
undark.description: Amid a national push to ease restrictions on certain peptides, California legislator Joe Patterson has introduced a state-level bill that would to establish a working group tasked with making recommendations to allow physicians and hospitals, among others, to prescribe and study promising peptides.

undark.title: Making Sense of Data From Wearable Health Trackers
undark.description: Wearable health devices such as smartwatches, glucose monitors, and sleep trackers are blurring the line between consumer wellness and clinical medicine. One physician argues that validation standards and privacy protections must be established to ensure the usefulness of the data these devices generate.

undark.title: In California, a Plan to Help Wildlife Cross a Busy Freeway
undark.description: The 101 freeway in California bisects a mountainous region where threatened cougars and other animals are blocked without a viable path across 10 lanes of heavily trafficked roadway. But an ambitious 210-foot “vegetated bridge” will soon be home to what organizers say is the largest wildlife crossing anywhere in the world.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

proj-syn.title: Is a European Single Market for Energy Such a Good Idea?
proj-syn.description: Although textbook microeconomics shows why less energy-market fragmentation would be better for Europe as a whole, that does not mean it would be a good deal for countries producing low-carbon electricity at minimal marginal cost. In fact, if more integration creates free riders, the political backlash could be profound.

proj-syn.title: China’s Failed Rebalancing
proj-syn.description: When China’s leaders first acknowledged the need to rebalance the economy nearly two decades ago, it seemed like a matter of when, not if. But with the household consumption share of Chinese GDP remaining stubbornly low, officials’ promises to boost domestic demand have lost all credibility.

proj-syn.title: Crowning a Healthy Populism
proj-syn.description: Although recent political mobilizations in Hungary, Albania, and other parts of Central and Eastern Europe could be described as populist and nationalist, they have little in common with the aggressive ethnonationalism that MAGA professes. Could they be a model for a new form of politics?

proj-syn.title: Why Rules-Based Orders Fail
proj-syn.description: For a brief period after the Cold War, Americans persuaded themselves that the liberal order had become self-sustaining. And yet, any rules-based system elaborate enough to govern and interpret its own operations will eventually confront questions that its rules cannot answer.

proj-syn.title: The Tide Is Turning Against Russia
proj-syn.description: With Ukraine reclaiming territory, mounting drone strikes deep in Russian territory, and draining Russia’s coffers, Vladimir Putin would do well to seek a negotiated freeze to the conflict. But there is no guarantee that he will, not least because he might not grasp the situation Russia is in.

proj-syn.title: Managing Sino-American Interdependence
proj-syn.description: At their summit last month, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping seemed to recognize that they are in the same boat. If either the United States or China tries to cripple or decouple from the other, it will harm its own firms, consumers, financial markets, and innovation ecosystem.

proj-syn.title: Who Gains in an AI-Supercharged Economy?
proj-syn.description: If AI delivers as promised and fundamentally transforms the economy, we will have moved from the current investment phase, where AI builders dominate, to one where AI users will reap the greatest reward. That is what happens every time an innovation becomes a general-purpose technology.

proj-syn.title: Development in a Time of Disruption
proj-syn.description: Once firms and economies ascend to market dominance, they often kick away the ladder behind them and erect barriers to market entry to stymie would-be challengers. But developing countries can and do leapfrog incumbent technologies, and conditions for doing so may be particularly favorable now.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Un-American Capitalism
proj-syn.description: The current US administration's openly corrupt style of crony capitalism is the antithesis of the institutional foundation on which the US economy was built. The winners in the new oligarchic competition are not those who make the best products, but rather those who are best at flattering the mad king.

proj-syn.title: Can the Manchester Model Save Britain?
proj-syn.description: Following a decades-long effort to lay the foundations for economic dynamism, Greater Manchester has become the UK’s fastest-growing region. While the Manchester model cannot be precisely replicated at the national level, it does carry important lessons for outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer's likely successor.

proj-syn.title: How Trillionaires Are Really Made
proj-syn.description: Some may argue that the world’s first trillionaire is a story of technological triumph and a win for American capitalism. But markets have not bet on cutting-edge technology or a company too big to fail, but rather on the idea of a mega-monopolist with wealth and influence so vast that the US government will not allow him to fail.

proj-syn.title: Cities Show How Climate Action Makes Life Better
proj-syn.description: Cities have shown that a combination of adaptation measures and energy efficiency can save lives, improve well-being, reduce energy costs, and create conditions for sustainable growth. A new partnership seeks to help mayors and city leaders scale up these efforts through technical and financial assistance.

proj-syn.title: The Myth of Global Chaos
proj-syn.description: Today’s seemingly nonstop international tumult is not as unintelligible as it seems. What pundits lazily describe as chaos is the culmination of developments that were long in the making and arrived at a time when the international system was no longer able to prevent or mitigate geopolitical shocks.

proj-syn.title: The Microfinance Debate Is Missing the Point
proj-syn.description: For too long, policymakers, economists, and investors have focused on whether microfinance actually helps people, reducing a complex issue to a meaningless yes-or-no verdict. The most important questions concern how loans are designed, delivered, and regulated, who receives them, and what they are used for.

proj-syn.title: Turning Latin America’s Resilience Into Growth
proj-syn.description: Economic stabilization has been a significant achievement for Latin America and the Caribbean, a region with a long history of financial crises. But these countries need a well-sequenced reform agenda to attract private investment and create the growth engine that will translate hard-won gains into higher living standards.
